beginner.summary: For business users and new consultants who must work on both sides of Dynamics 365, because clients use the name for the customer engagement (CRM) apps and for the finance and operations (ERP) apps. Covers the suite and licensing, Dataverse and model-driven apps, Sales, Customer Service, Field Service and Customer Insights, then Finance, Supply Chain Management and Business Central at user level, with views, dashboards, Power BI and Copilot, following the scope of the retired MB-910 and MB-920 exams.
prerequisites: Knows everyday sales, service, purchasing and accounting processes
Comfortable with web applications, Excel and Outlook
Trial or training environments for the customer engagement apps and for Finance and Supply Chain Management with the USMF demo company
outcomes: Explain the Dynamics 365 apps, their licences and where the CRM side ends and the ERP side begins
Run leads to orders, cases, work orders and segments in the customer engagement apps
Post journals, invoices, payments, purchase and sales orders and inventory movements in Finance and Supply Chain Management
Report with views, dashboards and Power BI and check Copilot output before using it

intermediate.summary: For functional consultants who can already use Dynamics 365 and now configure it on the customer engagement (CRM) side and on the finance and operations (ERP) side, since clients ask for both. Covers Dataverse tables, forms, views, business rules and security roles, Sales, Customer Service, unified routing, SLAs and Field Service configuration, Finance, Supply Chain Management and Business Central configuration, data migration, Power Automate inside Dynamics 365, Copilot and agent configuration and testing, mapped to the current MB-230, MB-310, MB-330, MB-800, AB-210 and AB-250 exams.
prerequisites: Can run sales, service, finance and supply chain transactions as a user
Knows Dataverse, model-driven apps and finance and operations navigation
Has administrator access to customer engagement and finance and operations sandboxes and a Business Central sandbox
outcomes: Customise Dataverse tables, forms, views, business rules and security roles inside solutions
Configure Sales, Customer Service routing and SLAs, and Field Service to client requirements
Configure legal entities, ledgers, posting, inventory, warehouses and policies in Finance and Supply Chain Management, and posting groups in Business Central
Migrate data, automate with Power Automate, configure Copilot and agents, and test the result

advanced.summary: For solution architects, technical leads and programme managers who design Dynamics 365 for clients that mean the customer engagement (CRM) apps, the finance and operations (ERP) apps or both. Covers solution architecture and fit-gap, environments after the Lifecycle Services freeze, ALM, dual-write, virtual tables and integration, plug-in and X++ extension models at architect level, performance, security and compliance, migration from Dynamics AX, NAV and CRM on-premises, Copilot and agents at scale, governance, licensing cost and programme leadership, with AB-100 as the architect exam since MB-700 retired.
prerequisites: Has configured or built Dynamics 365 customer engagement or finance and operations apps on at least one project
Knows Dataverse, solutions, data entities and security at consultant level
Leads design, integration or delivery decisions
outcomes: Design Dynamics 365 solutions across CRM, ERP and Business Central with environment and ALM strategies
Choose integration, extension and data patterns that hold up under volume and service updates
Plan secure, compliant migrations from Dynamics AX, NAV and CRM on-premises
Govern Copilot, agents, licences and cost, and lead programmes through go-live
